contents.text: The pronouns who and whoever are subject pronouns. They act as subjects of sentences or clauses. The pronouns whom and whomever are object pronouns. They act as objects of action verbs or prepositions.

header.text: To figure out whether to use who/whoever or whom/whomever, restate the sentence or clause with a personal pronoun. If the personal pronoun is a subject pronoun (he, she, or they), use who/whoever. If the personal pronoun is an object pronoun (him, her, or them), use whom/whomever.

The subject pronoun who should be used.
Peter, who/whom you met yesterday, has four brothers.
The object pronoun whom should be used.
